abstract: Maintains aerodynamic wind load ratings and mast foundation specifications
system_message:
You are the Structural engineering lead (STR), responsible for maintaining aerodynamic wind load ratings and mast foundation specifications across field observatory candidates.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Canada·Maintains aerodynamic wind load ratings and mast foundation specifications（SOIL）
information_points.content:
STR-SOIL-LNA：Under testing performed in Canada, the Paso Pehuenche Saddle Camp mast and antenna mountings demonstrated a structural wind gust resistance of 160 km/h evaluated at the maximum survivable 3-second wind gust velocity.
STR-SOIL-DAY：Testing conducted in Canada shows that the Valle de los Cóndores Plateau Outpost has a structural wind gust resistance of 140 km/h for its guyed sensor mast and antenna mountings against the maximum survivable 3-second wind gust velocity.
STR-SOIL-5V3：For the Laguna del Maule Caldera Rim Site, testing conducted in Canada recorded a structural wind gust resistance of 140 km/h for the guyed sensor mast and antenna mountings under maximum survivable 3-second wind gust conditions.

information_points.title: United States·Maintains aerodynamic wind load ratings and mast foundation specifications（AERO）
information_points.content:
STR-AERO-ZGT：For the Laguna del Maule Caldera Rim Site, testing conducted in the United States established that the guyed sensor mast and antenna mountings achieve a structural wind gust resistance of 200 km/h based on the maximum survivable 3-second wind gust velocity.
STR-AERO-G1Z：Evaluations performed in the United States indicate that the Valle de los Cóndores Plateau Outpost deployment features a structural wind gust resistance of 140 km/h on its guyed sensor mast and antenna mountings under maximum survivable 3-second wind gust velocities.
STR-AERO-E2B：Testing in the United States for the Paso Pehuenche Saddle Camp determined that the guyed sensor mast and antenna mountings possess a structural wind gust resistance of 160 km/h for the maximum survivable 3-second wind gust velocity.
